description: Revise all the important Operating Systems concepts and practice lots of MCQ questions to prepare for interviews.

modules.name: Process Management
modules.description: The coordination and control of executing programs (processes) within an operating system. It involves creating, suspending, resuming, and terminating processes, as well as managing their resources.

modules.name: Memory Management
modules.description: The allocation and deallocation of computer memory to running processes and the operating system itself. It includes techniques like virtual memory, paging, and segmentation to efficiently use available memory.

modules.name: File Systems
modules.description: The structure and organization of data storage on disk drives or other storage devices. File systems manage how data is stored, retrieved, and organized in files and directories.

modules.name: I/O Management
modules.description: The control and coordination of input/output operations between the computer and its peripheral devices. It involves device drivers, buffering, and managing data transfer between the CPU and I/O devices.

modules.name: Virtualization
modules.description: The creation of virtual versions of computer resources, such as hardware platforms, operating systems, or storage devices. It allows multiple virtual machines to run on a single physical machine, improving resource utilization.

modules.name: Scheduling Algorithms
modules.description: Methods used to determine the order in which processes are allocated CPU time. These algorithms aim to optimize system performance, fairness, and resource utilization.

problems_with_status.name: Addressing Starvation in Multilevel Queue Scheduling

modules.name: Concurrency and Synchronization
modules.description: The simultaneous execution of multiple processes or threads, and the mechanisms to coordinate their actions. This includes techniques like mutual exclusion, semaphores, and monitors to prevent race conditions and ensure data integrity.
